In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new synthetic routes for the preparation of amavadins and their structural characterization.
the development of a new type of water oxidation catalyst, which is based on the redox-active NO ligand.

the discovery of the first water-oxidizing complexes of early transition metals and the identification of the first vanadium complex that does not contain the V=O moiety, and that can mediate the oxidation to dioxygen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

amavadin and related complexes are not only the first vanadium-containing biomolecules with a potential role in water oxidation, but also the first biomolecules of any metal to be shown to be capable of catalyzing this reaction.
amavadin and related complexes are able to catalyze the oxidation of water, although with a low rate.
the V(V)-{NOṄ<} moiety in amavadin is not the active site for water oxidation, as it has previously been suggested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vanadium(V)-{O=NOṄ<} group is a good model of the V(V)=O group in the amavadin family of complexes and that both are capable of water oxidation.
amavadin and related compounds are promising candidates for the development of new catalysts for the oxygen-evolution reaction (OER).
the vanadium complexes with the N-hydroxyimine ligand, HIDA, and its analogues are the first recognized early transition-metal complexes to mediate the oxidation reaction of water to dioxygen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amavadins, and their synthetic models, are not just interesting natural products but also promising catalysts for the oxidation of water.
the amavadin motif is not essential to the catalytic activity of vanadium in water oxidation, which is instead due to a combination of the vanadium center and the oxyimino ligand.

amavadin and its homologues are not only the first known vanadium(IV)-mediated catalysts of water oxidation but are also the first examples of the early transition-metal complexes that can mediate this reaction.
